requirements.requirement: The system must render a side-by-side layout displaying at least two providers simultaneously.
The system must display each provider in a distinct column with consistent structure across all providers.
The system must display provider identity information (e.g., name and specialty) at the top of each column.
The system must display an overall score for each provider in a prominent and visually comparable format.
The system must render a breakdown of individual measures for each provider aligned row-wise across columns.
The system must visually highlight the highest value for each measure across providers.
The system must visually indicate lower-performing values for each measure relative to peers.
The system must support rendering of more than two providers without breaking layout or alignment.
The system must maintain horizontal alignment of measures across all provider columns.
The system must use reusable component structure consistent with existing frontend component patterns.
The system must render visual indicators (e.g., color, icons, or badges) for strengths and weaknesses per measure.
The system must gracefully handle missing measure data by displaying a neutral placeholder without breaking layout.
The system must render consistently when providers have unequal numbers of measures by preserving alignment and filling gaps appropriately.
The system must support responsive layout that adapts to smaller screen sizes without loss of critical comparison information.
The system must render within acceptable performance thresholds (e.g., under 200ms for initial component render with up to 5 providers).
The system must accept input data conforming to the schema defined in EVAL-COMPARE-UX-S1 without runtime errors.
The system must correctly reflect normalized and ranked values produced by EVAL-COMPARE-UX-S2 without altering underlying scores.
The system must display a clear visual distinction between providers when two providers have identical scores for a measure.
The system must render an empty state message when fewer than two providers are provided.
The system must not crash or throw uncaught errors when provided with null or malformed input data.
